context.description: Slug of the bounded context the service belongs to. A .proto knows its package, not which context owns it. Defaults to the name of the input directory; not read when external is set.

service.description: Slug of the service that publishes or calls these protos. Defaults to the name of the input directory; not read when external is set.

paths.description: Directories of protos this service publishes, relative to the input root. They become what it provides. A directory fetch-bsr wrote carries its lock, and the lock says which module the protos came from. With external set, the copy vendored beside the adapter that calls the external, and what it provides is what the external answers on.

vendored.description: Directories of client copies this service consumes, relative to the input root. They become what it calls. Listed rather than globbed: which copies a service may keep is a boundary a reviewer should see change.

peers.description: Which service answers for a vendored copy, as the proto package to its service id. A package with no line here is called as unknown and its steps stay unresolved.

modules.description: Which module a directory's protos belong to, as the directory relative to the input root to the module id. Only needed where there is no lock beside them to say.

defs.description: Whether a message imported from another file is promoted to a shared type, on the reasoning that the import is the author's own signal it is not local.

external.description: Id of a system outside the estate the protos under paths belong to, when it is not one of ours: a copy vendored beside the adapter that calls it, read for what the third party answers on. A bare name with no dot, the same one the caller's extractor is given under externals. Set, the fragment carries the external and no service, and context, service, vendored, peers and modules are not read.

externalName.description: What the external is called on the page.

externalSummary.description: A sentence or two on what the estate uses it for.

externalUrl.description: Where the third party documents itself, for a reader who needs more than the vendored copy.

out.description: Name of the fragment file, inside the step's output directory.
